Before proceeding further, it may also be noticed here that t

he learned Reference Court after having gone through the entire material on record has recorded a positive finding of fact with respect to the locational and potential advantage attached to the acquired land, land, the same being located exactly ly on the G.T. Road about 1 km.
km from Pipli towards Karnal; on the eastern side.
It was also noticed that across G.T. Road towards western side and just infront of the acquired land,, Sectors 2 and 3 of the Urban Estate, Kurukshetra existed.
The learned Reference Court also recorded that the land under acquisition was having potential for being used as residential, industrial as well as commercial purpose.

Paragraph Nos.8, 9 and 13 of the impugned Award of learned Reference Court being relevant releva are extracted hereunder:-
hereunder:

"8. At the very outset, it is pertinent to mention here that admittedly the acquired land earlier belonged to the petitioners and the same is situated on the G.T. Road, on its east side, about 1 K.M. from Pipli and towards Karnal, and that across the G.T.
Road in the West side just in front of the Karnal,
3 of 8 acquired land, are situated Sector-2 Sector 2 and Sector 3 of the Urban Estate, developed by the Haryana Urban Development Authority, (for short, HUDA), Kurukshetra.
9.

Further, undisputed position emerging from the evidence brought on record is that the acquired land is situated on the East side of the G.T. road at 'T' point where the road coming, inter inter-alia,
alia, between Sectors 2 and 3 joins the G.T. Road, that just near th thee acquired land towards North is situated Rice-Sheller Rice Sheller abutting the G.T. Road, and on the South side of the acquired land F.C.I. Godown are also situated nearby, which also abuts the G.T. Road; and that on Pipli-Ladwa Pipli Ladwa Road, there are shops.

Other buildings and locations i.e. New Grain Market, Pipli, shown in the site site-plan, plan, Exh. P2 which is proved by PW 2 Ram Sarup,
Retired Patwari, are situated far- far away from the acquired land.

However, in view of the above position it is proved that the acquired land being situated just on the G.T. Road, on the East side thereof and on the West side of the G.T. Road, there are situated Sectors 2 and 3 of HUDA.

In that view of the matter, as held in Shrimati Uma and others Versus The Tribunal Constituted under the Punjab Town Improvement Act, 192, Jullundhur and others, 1979 P.L.R. 551, such land has potential for residential purposes.

Moreover,, the sale deeds Ex.P-11 11 and Ex.P-6 Ex.P 6 pertain to the revenue estate of village Pipli, whereas the acquisition in the case in hand is from village Bir Pipli, as such in the absence of there being any proof of locational and potential similarity between the two revenue estates of villages Bir Pipli and Pipli, no reliance can be placed upon Ex.P- Ex.P 11 and Ex.P-6.

As regards sale deeds Ex.R-11 to Ex.R Ex.R-3 3 which are though prior to the date of acquisition in the case in hand and are even geographically located in close proximity to the acquired land forming part of same revenue estate of village Bir Pipli, yet are liable to be ignored ignore in the wake of deposition made by PW PW-5 5 Sh.

Even the learned Reference Court having acknowledged ed the similarity of location and potential of the land forming part of Ex.P-7 7 in comparison to the acquired land, went on to rely upon the same, however wrongly applied the average of sale instances Ex.P Ex.P-7 and Ex.R-1 to Ex.R-3 3 which was wholly uncalled for, fo as the sale instances Ex.R Ex.R-1 to Ex.R-3 were not reflecting the genuine sale price or the representative market value value.

7) needs to be taken into account as the best available sale exemplar for the purposes of determination of market value of the acquired land land..

 Rs. per acre.
